To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a database can be represented in negative form using a number of records that is only logarithmic in the number of original records, and that this negative form can be used to answer membership queries in time no worse then linear in the negative representation size.

negative representations can be used to reduce the amount of information stored about individuals, and that negative representations are a feasible way to reduce the amount that an individual can be identified.

a database consisting n l-bit records can, in principle, be represented negatively using O(ln) records, that reconstructing the original database given the negative representation is an NP-hard, and that the time complexity of processing a membership query against the negative representation is linear in the size of the negative representation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of whether a negative database can be used as a privacy-preserving representation for a database, that is, whether it is possible to use a negative database to protect a database from disclosure.
the question: can a negative representation of a database be constructed so that membership queries for that database can be processed efficiently?
the problem of enhancing privacy by using negative representations of data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
negative representation is a promising approach to enhancing privacy.
negative representations of data are feasible, can enhance privacy, and can be useful in some applications.
a negative representation of a database can be constructed in time polynomial in n but exponential in l, but the size of the negative representation is only linear in n and logarithmic in l.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a negative representation of data can provide an effective way for enhancing privacy, but at the same time, the problem of reconstructing the original data from a negative representation is NP-complete, so it may not be easy to do so.
the negative representation scheme is feasible, but it is not a panacea for privacy problems.
a database can be represented by a negative representation of its complement set.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a negative representation can be used to provide privacy protection for a data owner while allowing authorized users to perform queries on the data.
a negative representation of data can be used for enhancing privacy, and that the negative database representation is a feasible alternative to traditional database representation.
negative representation of data is a feasible and potentially effective means of enhancing privacy.
